method: Static second review: SHA-256 verification, atomscan, cleave facts and decoded strings, rizin control-flow/call-argument tracing, and offline resource/archive extraction. No specimen executed or contacted.

evidence: All three variants are executable module-level Python statements, with no quoting or test harness. Each constructs a socket, connects, and duplicates that same socket descriptor onto stdin/stdout/stderr before launching a shell.

Line 1 connects to 10.0.0.1:4242 and spawns /bin/bash through pty.spawn. Line 3 invokes subprocess.call([/bin/sh,-i]) after the same redirection. Line 5 obtains its endpoint from RHOST/RPORT, loops over descriptors 0/1/2, and spawns /bin/sh through a PTY.

Sequential execution matters: the first shell blocks; later variants can run after it returns. A failed connection can terminate the script. These limitations do not remove the remote-shell functionality.
samples.balance: Private addressing and recipe-like repetition permit an assessment or demonstration origin, but no supplied packaging or deployment context establishes one. A standalone file on a machine provides an immediately usable outbound shell; that behavior tips the judgment.
samples.traits: Retained accurate existing reverse-shell and neutral capability coverage; no added identity or endpoint-based conviction.

samples.identification: Urelas MSMP-profile concealed executable loader (modified Run-value near miss)
evidence: WinMain at VA 0x401081 reaches initialization at 0x40128b. The resource staging path at 0x402432 calls 0x402974, which uses FindResourceW/SizeofResource/LoadResource/LockResource on resource 131, then passes that buffer and its size to 0x402278. That helper extracts the archive, appends generated padding, and stores the output through 0x408bfe. The caller ShellExecuteW launches the same destination at 0x4025e6.

The ZIP resource was carved using the PE resource table. The archive constructor at 0x407b91 sets the password to 1234. Offline decryption and decompression recover HanAgent_pe.exe, 228352 bytes, SHA-256 0742a171ff4693bb30cd153ca77039b1012b867ed7fa4aef30be00526ee55678. It is another PE with a PECompact2 bootstrap; its full unpacked behavior was not established and is not needed for the parent verdict.

The 0x408b07 state reader tries configuration files, complements each byte of a 512-byte record, and verifies MSMP at 0x408b65. This is a deliberate transformed state record rather than an entropy-based inference.

The cleanup function at 0x403141 obtains its own module path, formats that path into a del/if-exist/goto loop, writes a batch script, and ShellExecuteA launches it hidden. It removes the parent image, attempts directory removal, and deletes the script itself.

At 0x402245 the registry value passed to RegSetValueExW is Xun, under Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows. Xun is not the platform Run value. TrayKey at 0x402627 is used for event bookkeeping. No Run-write persistence claim is justified for this file; the persistence trait correctly stays absent.

Resource 130 is a separate 205-byte real-mode BIOS disk loader. Disassembly in 16-bit mode shows relocation from 07c0:0000 to 0800:0000, INT 13h reads including an extended read, and far transfers to 8000:0000 or 07c0:0000. No reachable installation of resource 130 was established; its presence does not prove boot persistence.
samples.balance: Encrypted resource-to-process delivery, transformed state, network configuration, and self-image cleanup jointly establish a covert loader. Ordinary installers can extract and launch programs, but the complete traced configuration/cleanup profile supports the malicious judgment. The collector filename and missing registry persistence are not verdict evidence.
samples.traits: Added notable metadata/binary/resource/boot-loader::bios-read-far-transfer for the previously unreported BIOS code content; retained accurate hostile coverage and absent Run persistence.

evidence: The DLL exports hook (a no-op) and hook2. DllMain reaches application initialization at 0x1000a830, which starts worker threads and installs process-creation hooks in configured branches. The hook2 export enables SeDebugPrivilege and calls 0x10005eb0.

0x10005eb0 enumerates processes to select explorer.exe, opens that PID, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path into it, resolves LoadLibraryA, and supplies that function and the remote path to CreateRemoteThread. This is a traced DLL-injection path, not an API-name-only inference.

CKeyboardManager initialization at 0x1000e4d0 schedules the 0x1000e290 polling worker. The worker calls GetAsyncKeyState and tests its pressed bit, handles modifier states/key labels, and sends text to 0x1000e050. 0x1000e180 adds the foreground window title and a timestamp to the record.

0x1000e050 obtains a writable file handle through resolved CreateFileA, XORs record bytes with 0x62 into the same buffer passed to the indirect write at 0x1000e14f, and closes the handle. The indirect target is proven: 0x1002b6a0 resolves WriteFile and stores its address into 0x100408a8, the exact slot used by the recorder.

0x10010a30 resolves OpenClipboard, obtains CF_TEXT through GetClipboardData(1), sizes and locks that handle, allocates a tagged record, copies the text into record+1, unlocks/closes the clipboard, and hands that record to 0x1000e840 and then the connection buffer routine at 0x10001c20. The capture rule does not depend on a speculative full network-exfiltration relationship.

The class-layout evidence spans keyboard, screen, shell, kernel, registry, file, and system managers. This corroborates Gh0st lineage alongside implemented input recording; version strings claiming Microsoft are self-attestation, not verified authorship.
samples.balance: Surreptitious foreground-window/key logging, XOR log storage, tagged clipboard capture, and Explorer DLL injection outweigh generic remote-administration uses. No authorized administration/testing context is supplied. The VirusTotal report was not used to establish any behavior or select the verdict.
samples.traits: Retained accurate existing input-recording, clipboard-capture, family-layout and neutral primitive coverage.

rule_placement: metadata/binary/resource/boot-loader records embedded BIOS loader code in .rsrc; firmware images and host-executed instructions are separate subjects. No sample-selected names, endpoints, exact sizes or hashes gate the new trait.
controls: check.py generates two positive resource-section code examples varying disk, sector, segment and padding, plus six near misses covering interrupt, disk operation, transfer instruction, missing call, ordinary data, and non-resource placement. The trait is notable in positive controls.
limitations: Static reachability and call arguments establish capabilities, not successful deployment. No registry origin, user authorization, installation history, or live endpoint state was supplied.

checks_completed.sha256: All three supplied SHA-256 hashes matched.
checks_completed.rescans: atomscan re-run on all three original paths. Exact YAML finding delta: one notable BIOS-code trait added to the EXE; no removals or severity changes.
checks_completed.run_persistence: No objectives/persistence trait fires on the Xun-value EXE.
